The Dutch job market is full of opportunities but figuring out where to begin can still feel like a lot. You might be adjusting your CV to a new format, trying to understand what employers expect, or sending out applications and hearing nothing back.  Why many expats choose to work with a recruitment agency When you're new to a country, you're not just job hunting but also learning how things work. At Abroad Experience, the process is personal. It starts with a conversation about your background, your strengths, and what kind of role you're actually looking for. From there, we match you with opportunities that fit not just on paper, but in terms of work culture and expectations too.  It's about finding the right job, not just any job One of the biggest frustrations for expats is spending weeks applying to roles without really knowing if they're a good fit. Working with a recruitment agency changes that. Instead of sending your CV into the void, you're being introduced to companies that are actively looking for someone with your profile. Abroad Experience focuses on multilingual professionals and international work environments, where English is often the main working language. That means you don't always need Dutch to get started  Support that makes a difference Interviews in a new country can feel a little intimidating, especially when you're not sure what's expected from you. What kind of questions will they ask? How direct should you be? What does a good answer look like in a Dutch work environment? Before your interview, you'll typically get a preparation call with practical insights about the company, the team, and what they're looking for.
